title: Impact of BRT Corridor on Urban Commute Times

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with two-way fixed effects (unit and period), complemented by an event-study for pre-trend diagnostics.
- Why: The data comprise treated and control urban areas observed before and after the BRT opening with a clear treated × post indicator. DID isolates the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) under standard panel assumptions.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of the BRT, the log commute times of treated and control areas would have evolved in parallel.
  - No spillovers/Stable composition: Treatment in a treated area does not affect outcomes in controls; the set of areas is stable.
  - No anticipation: Treated units do not adjust commute times in advance of the opening.
  - Common treatment timing (as encoded by post) or appropriate alignment in the event-study.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load packages (install if missing)
pkgs <- c("fixest", "sandwich", "lmtest")
for (p in pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}
library(fixest)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s48_data.csv"
df <- read.csv(path)

# Ensure types
df$unit_id <- as.integer(df$unit_id)
df$period  <- as.integer(df$period)
df$treated <- as.integer(df$treated)
df$post    <- as.integer(df$post)
df$treat_x_post <- as.integer(df$treat_x_post)
df$y <- as.numeric(df$y)

# Sanity check: enforce treat_x_post = treated * post
if (any(df$treat_x_post != df$treated * df$post, na.rm = TRUE)) {
  warning("treat_x_post inconsistent with treated*post. Recomputing.")
}
df$treat_x_post <- df$treated * df$post

# Create a clean period index for trends/event-study
# (in case 'period' has gaps or is not 1..T)
df$period_num <- as.integer(factor(df$period))

# Helper to print a DID effect cleanly
print_effect <- function(name, est, se){
  z <- est / se
  p <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(z)))
  ci_low <- est - 1.96 * se
  ci_high <- est + 1.96 * se
  pct <- 100 * (exp(est) - 1)
  pct_low <- 100 * (exp(ci_low) - 1)
  pct_high <- 100 * (exp(ci_high) - 1)
  cat(sprintf("\n[%s]\n", name))
  cat(sprintf("  Coef (log points): %.4f\n", est))
  cat(sprintf("  SE: %.4f | z: %.2f | p-value: %.4f\n", se, z, p))
  cat(sprintf("  95%% CI (log points): [%.4f, %.4f]\n", ci_low, ci_high))
  cat(sprintf("  Implied percent effect: %.2f%% (95%% CI: [%.2f%%, %.2f%%])\n",
              pct, pct_low, pct_high))
}

cat("Difference-in-Differences: Impact of BRT on log commute times (y)\n")

# 2) Baseline DID (pooled OLS with treated, post, interaction)
m_ols <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
vc_ols <- sandwich::vcovHC(m_ols, type = "HC1")
co_ols <- coef(m_ols)["treat_x_post"]
se_ols <- sqrt(diag(vc_ols))["treat_x_post"]

# 3) Preferred TWFE DID (unit and period fixed effects, clustered by unit)
m_twfe <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = df, cluster = ~ unit_id)
co_twfe <- coef(m_twfe)["treat_x_post"]
se_twfe <- sqrt(vcov(m_twfe)["treat_x_post","treat_x_post"])

# 4) Robustness: two-way clustering (unit and period)
m_twfe_2c <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = df, cluster = ~ unit_id + period)
co_twfe_2c <- coef(m_twfe_2c)["treat_x_post"]
se_twfe_2c <- sqrt(vcov(m_twfe_2c)["treat_x_post","treat_x_post"])

# 5) Robustness: unit-specific linear trends
# fixest supports FE with slopes using the ^ operator: unit_id^period_num
m_trend <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period + unit_id^period_num, data = df, cluster = ~ unit_id)
co_trend <- coef(m_trend)["treat_x_post"]
se_trend <- sqrt(vcov(m_trend)["treat_x_post","treat_x_post"])

# 6) Event-study for pre-trend diagnostics
# Identify the first post period (common treatment time)
if (any(df$post == 1)) {
  t0 <- min(df$period[df$post == 1], na.rm = TRUE)
} else {
  t0 <- NA_integer_
}
if (!is.na(t0)) {
  df$rel_time <- df$period - t0
  # Event-study with ref period = -1 (the period just before opening)
  m_es <- feols(y ~ i(rel_time, treated, ref = -1) | unit_id + period, data = df, cluster = ~ unit_id)

  # Extract pre-trend coefficients (rel_time < -1)
  coefs_es <- coef(m_es)
  nms <- names(coefs_es)
  # pattern "rel_time::k:treated"
  get_rel <- function(s) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("rel_time::(-?\\d+):treated", "\\1", s)))
  is_rel <- grepl("^rel_time::(-?\\d+):treated$", nms)
  rel_vals <- sapply(nms[is_rel], get_rel)
  pre_names <- nms[is_rel][rel_vals < -1]
  pre_test <- NA
  if (length(pre_names) > 0) {
    pre_test <- wald(m_es, pre_names)
  }
}

# 7) Placebo test: use only pre-periods, split pre into early vs late "placebo_post"
df_pre <- subset(df, post == 0)
placebo_pval <- NA
if (nrow(df_pre) > 0) {
  pre_periods <- sort(unique(df_pre$period))
  if (length(pre_periods) >= 2) {
    cutoff <- pre_periods[ceiling(length(pre_periods)/2)]
    df_pre$placebo_post <- as.integer(df_pre$period >= cutoff)
    df_pre$treat_x_placebo <- df_pre$treated * df_pre$placebo_post
    m_placebo <- feols(y ~ treat_x_placebo | unit_id + period, data = df_pre, cluster = ~ unit_id)
    co_pl <- coef(m_placebo)["treat_x_placebo"]
    se_pl <- sqrt(vcov(m_placebo)["treat_x_placebo","treat_x_placebo"])
    z_pl <- co_pl / se_pl
    placebo_pval <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(z_pl)))
  }
}

# 8) Print key numerical results
print_effect("Baseline DID (pooled OLS, HC1 SE)", co_ols, se_ols)
print_effect("Preferred DID (TWFE, clustered by unit)", co_twfe, se_twfe)
print_effect("Robustness: TWFE with two-way clustering (unit & period)", co_twfe_2c, se_twfe_2c)
print_effect("Robustness: TWFE with unit-specific linear trends", co_trend, se_trend)

if (exists("m_es")) {
  cat("\n[Event-study pre-trend test]\n")
  if (!is.null(pre_test) && !is.na(pre_test$wald)) {
    cat(sprintf("  H0: All pre-treatment (<= -2) coefficients = 0 | F-stat: %.2f | p-value: %.4f\n",
                pre_test$wald, pre_test$p.value))
  } else {
    cat("  Insufficient pre-period variation to test pre-trends.\n")
  }
}

if (!is.na(placebo_pval)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n[Placebo DID in pre-periods]\n  p-value on placebo interaction: %.4f (should be large under parallel trends)\n",
              placebo_pval))
}

# 9) Final, clear numerical result (ATT from preferred TWFE)
att <- co_twfe
att_se <- se_twfe
att_ci <- c(att - 1.96*att_se, att + 1.96*att_se)
att_pct <- 100*(exp(att)-1)

cat("\n==== Final ATT (Preferred TWFE) ====\n")
cat(sprintf("ATT (log points): %.4f | 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", att, att_ci[1], att_ci[2]))
cat(sprintf("Implied percent change in commute time: %.2f%%\n", att_pct))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. A BRT corridor should reduce commute times due to dedicated lanes and improved service reliability, implying a decrease in log commute times for treated areas.
- Magnitude: A plausible ATT is around −0.05 to −0.20 log points, i.e., roughly a 5% to 20% reduction in commute times, depending on baseline congestion, BRT design quality, and network integration. Robustness checks (two-way clustering, unit trends, and pre-trend tests) should not overturn the negative sign if parallel trends holds.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in commute times between treated and untreated areas over time.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The opening of a BRT corridor is associated with an increase in the log of commute times.
